Comments: I haven't had time or a currently active (paid subscription/computer access) method by which I can search literature to find out, but would be interested in knowing how accurate people's self descriptions of things asked in a survey such as this one, (and prior one from the same researcher that I recall too),  match up with real world measurements of the same.  For instance, if a person says they are or are not aware of being ticklish, is there a physical test of sensitivity of their skin areas, how close do they recognize touching in two areas on the arm, lets say, are close to each other?  Does it feel like two separate touches, or one touch?  And at which point do different people perceive the two separated touches to be one touch?   I remember decades ago reading about studies that, before Internet surveys, they did actual testing to find out these qualities, like the ability to breathe and forget something (I think they were shown a box, and box lid was lifted showing in a transparent box a spider or disgusting thing and how well their rating of that being horrific or scared of it in their mind/abstract thought, vs when they actually encountered that, or viewing the cockroach scurrying across the floor.  Also,  you  didn't ask (maybe by zip code?) if people come from environment, or socio-economic area where seeing mice, cockroaches is common vs very uncommon.  I have witnessed very different reactions between myself and neighbors who react differently to both of these factors!
